name: polaris_ui_session_host
logic_name: Frontend-neutral offline session host (OfflineSession, routed submit, kernel-free queries)

test_list.description: submit("plan tomorrow") records UserInputSubmitted and next_record resolves its exact text with RecordTextKind::UserInput.
submit("$websearch(on)") commits DirectiveApplied (RecordTextKind::Directive), never a user input record.
A directive mixed with prose, a mention or a slash command is not a lone directive and is recorded verbatim as user input.
Text the directive grammar rejects is treated as prose and recorded verbatim; apply_directive itself still rejects it.
Whitespace-only input is rejected by the kernel and leaves no user input record.
After the owning kernel shuts down, the standalone list_sessions reads the registry and includes the session; limit is honoured.
session_exists is true for a created session and false for an unknown id, with no kernel running.
Close, reopen the same id and the typed text replays through next_record in order with the directive.
A recorded user message is not indexed yet so search finds nothing; a message indexed directly in the registry is found; an oversize query is an error.
SessionHostError displays exactly the underlying message for Ui and Unavailable.
Moved from polaris-cli: a cancelled next_record keeps the pending record and joins one CAS read.
Moved from polaris-cli: a failed CAS owner is reported once and close does not await it again.
Moved from polaris-cli: other-session payloads stay unresolved even when their blob is missing.
Debug-build wall time of OfflineSession::open over five runs is printed as min/median/max; it asserts only that every open succeeds.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: One submitted line: a lone directive or free typed text.

output_description: Receipt for the committed record; ordered resolved records carry bounded UTF-8 text and its kind.
